correctness.rationale: The analytic reduction is valid. Choosing \(q\mathbb Z^2\subset\Lambda\) gives a finite residue decomposition and an exact heat kernel whose Laurent coefficients reproduce \(c_{2,\Lambda}=1/(h\log r\log s)\) and the stated boundary coefficients. For nonzero residue classes, one Euler–Maclaurin step reduces the shifted double zeta to finitely many Hurwitz-zeta terms plus a holomorphic remainder on \(\Re z>-1\), giving the same vertical-strip control as the unrestricted lattice. The \(n\)-th-prime expansion has the identical second-order perturbation structure; shellwise domination by the full quadrant makes the remainder locally uniformly summable. The full primary two-generator proof was inspected: its Mellin contour shift, Ingham hypotheses and saddle expansion depend exactly on these Laurent and strip inputs, so substituting the finite-index data yields the displayed strong equivalent. The collision map \((a,b,c)\mapsto(qa+c,qb+c)\) has image exactly \(A\equiv B\pmod q\) with a unique residue \(c\), proving the deduplication corollary. The symbolic verifier independently checks the heat coefficients and finite collision identities.
risks: No uniformity in a growing lattice index is proved.
The proof assumes the underlying bases \(r,s\) are multiplicatively independent before the explicit collision construction.
